hook.line: 'Last Saturday' and 'next Saturday' are how you place a story or a plan on the calendar. In Spanish one small word, and where you put it, does the job.
hook.es: El fin de semana pasado vendimos trescientos tintos.
hook.en: Last weekend we sold three hundred black coffees.

examples.es: El sábado pasado compré flores en Paloquemao.
examples.en: Last Saturday I bought flowers at Paloquemao.
We didn't go out last week.

examples.es: El año pasado Tomás vivió en Toronto.
examples.en: Last year Tomás lived in Toronto.

examples.es: El próximo sábado vamos a bailar.
examples.en: Next Saturday we're going to dance.

examples.es: La próxima semana empiezo un curso.
examples.en: Next week I start a course.

examples.es: El jueves voy a comprar pan.
examples.en: On Thursday I'm going to buy bread.

rule:
For 'last', put *pasado* after the time word. It agrees with it: *el sábado pasado*, *la semana pasada*.

For 'next', put *próximo* in front: *el próximo año*, *la próxima semana*. You'll also hear *la semana que viene*, which means the same.

A day on its own doesn't set the time; the verb does. *El jueves compré pan* is last Thursday. *El jueves voy a comprar pan* is this coming one.

Only *hoy*, *ayer* and *mañana* fix the time by themselves.
smallPrint: *Pasado* and *próximo* are adjectives here, so they take *-a* with *la* words like *semana*.

options: We didn't go out last week.
We're not going out next week.

readAndPick.es: La próxima semana empiezo un curso.
options: I started a course last week.
I start a course next week.
I'm going to buy bread on Thursday.

The taxi drivers arrive next Monday.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *La semana ___ trabajé mucho.* (*pasado* or *pasada*)
Pick and type the whole sentence: *El ___ año voy a viajar.* (*pasado* or *próximo*)
yourTurn.answer: El próximo año voy a viajar.
yourTurn.why: *Voy a* is a plan, so 'next': *próximo*, in front.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Last Saturday I bought flowers.
yourTurn.why: *Pasado* goes after *sábado*, and *compré* is the past.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask a friend: did you travel last year?
yourTurn.why: 'Last year' is *el año pasado*, with a past verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Next week we're going to open on Sunday.
yourTurn.answer: La próxima semana vamos a abrir el domingo.
yourTurn.why: *Próxima* before *semana*, and *vamos a* for the plan.

yourTurn.prompt: Turn it into a plan for next Sunday: *El domingo pasado cociné.*
yourTurn.answer: El próximo domingo voy a cocinar.
yourTurn.why: Swap *pasado* for *próximo* in front, and move the verb into the future.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about last week: *La próxima semana voy a trabajar mucho.*
yourTurn.why: *Pasada* goes after *semana*, and the verb goes into the past.

pitfalls.why: *Pasado* comes after the time word; it's *próximo* that goes in front.

pitfalls.right: La próxima semana voy a trabajar mucho.
pitfalls.why: *Próxima* points forward, so the verb has to point forward too.

personal: Write one thing you did last weekend with *el sábado pasado* or *el domingo pasado*, and one plan with *la próxima semana*.
